newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity Magellan raised stock holdings in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Magellan raised stock holdings in Oct.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said its Magellan fund raised stock holdings to 89.8 percent of total assets at the end of October from 88.9 percent at the end of September.

According to Fidelity's latest monthly mutual fund guide, released on Wednesday, the massive mutual fund continued to cut holdings in bonds, trimming them to 8.7 percent of assets at October 31 from 9.8 percent at September 30.
Assets in cash and other investments rose slightly to 1.5 percent from 1.2 percent, while foreign investments slipped slightly to 11.6 percent from 11.7 percent.
Magellan's assets rose to $55.9 billion at the end of November from $53.2 billion at the end of October, according to the fund guide.

Magellan fund manager Robert Stanksy added Conrail Inc to his top 10 holdings, and cut Deere & Co from the list. U.S. Treasury notes maturing in 2005 and paying 5.875 percent remained at the top of the list.
Also in the top 10 were Intel Corp, Chrysler Corp , General Motors Corp, Caterpillar Inc, CSX Corp, Royal Dutch Petroleum Co, General Electric Co, and IBM Corp.
Magellan's investments in technology companies rose to 11.6 percent of total assets at the end of October, the most recent date available, from 10.1 percent at the end of September.
Energy companies remained the top sector, accounting for 14.0 percent of total assets at the end of October, versus 13.1 percent at the end of September.

Durable stocks slipped slightly to 10.3 percent of assets from 10.6 percent, finance shares rose to 8.6 percent from 7.6 percent, and industrial machinery and equipment fell to 8.4 percent from 9.7 percent.

Stansky added health care stocks to his holdings in October, and cut his stake in construction companies. Health care stocks accounted for 3.3 percent of assets at the end of October versus nil at the end of September.
Construction company stocks fell to nil at the end of October from 3.1 percent at the end of September.
Stansky was named portfolio manager of the closely-watched fund, the largest in the United States, in late May, after former fund manager Jeffrey Vinik suddenly announced his resignation.
Vinik's exit came after months of criticism from Magellan watchers, critical of his large investments in bonds, cash and cyclical stocks.
